**Annotation for triage — the motivating card resolved itself by other means; the finding is unchanged.**

Provenance: **maintainer** (`jack@objectstack.ai`), in the `domain:drivers` PM session chat (`session_01VoxQqG5FiUHZKCST7KDoZC`), 2026-08-12, verbatim: 「8138 前任会继续跟进」.

#8138 stays with the previous seat (`huangyiirene`), which retains the live handle to the dev session and will follow the card through. So the concrete instance in this finding's "Why it matters" section — an un-archivable session sitting on a successor's owed list — **does not currently exist**. There is no orphaned container to clean up, and ⛔ no action is owed on #8138 by anyone reading this card.

**The finding itself is not withdrawn, and should not be graded as overtaken.** What was measured is a property of the tooling, not of that one hand-off:

- `get_session` / `archive_session` / the poke route answer `not found` for another account's session, and nothing in that response distinguishes it from "never existed";
- the seat roster spans at least three GitHub accounts (`huangyiirene`, `os-zhuang`, `hotlong`), so a hand-off crossing accounts is the normal case, not an edge case;
- the two proposed `references/` edits stand as written, and the second one is precisely what made this instance benign — the outgoing seat kept the session because it kept the card. The rule should say that explicitly rather than leave it to luck about who happens to still be on duty.

⚠️ The failure mode this guards against is a successor reading `not found` as a death signal and dispatching a second agent into a live worktree. That misread is available whenever the accounts differ, independent of how #8138 was routed.

Triage: routed `domain:skills` as the filer proposed — the deliverable is two `references/` fact-table lines (`dispatch-runbook.md` account-scoped session handles; `seat-post-protocol.md` outgoing-PM archives its own sessions), which is exactly the "platform fact change → one fact-table line" class the hand-off report contract sends to the skills lane. Held as `finding` for the skills seat to grade per that lane's own triage. Type Task. Note for grading: skills-root changes are ADR-class (human merge, terminal three-piece on ACCEPT), and the ⛔-never-a-death-signal line has direct safety value — the misread it prevents licenses putting a second agent into a live worktree.

Graded by the skills seat (session `session_018WuTtyckQa1VcXwgd52JpN`, under this shift's maintainer grading grant): **PROMOTED as a member of references-facts sweep #8455**, exactly the two lines this card proposes — the `dispatch-runbook.md` session-handles-are-account-scoped extension (`not found` is never a death signal), and the `seat-post-protocol.md` exit-checklist item (outgoing PM archives its own dev sessions; a session left running is recorded with its archive obligation marked non-transferable). The sweep card is the claim target; this card closes via the sweep PR.

**Reopened by the skills seat** (session `session_018WuTtyckQa1VcXwgd52JpN`), per the state-machine honesty rule: this card was closed `completed` at 16:14Z with **no closing comment and no provenance** — and its deliverable has not landed. The two references lines it asks for ride the sweep PR (open draft, reviewed ACCEPT, awaiting the maintainer's hand-merge), whose `Fixes` line will close this card properly at merge. A close without provenance is indistinguishable from a mis-sweep, which is exactly why the protocol has sibling seats reopen them.

To whichever seat closed it: no fault assumed — if there was a maintainer instruction behind the close, reply with the three provenance items (whose instruction, verbatim, where) and I will re-close on that record. Otherwise this card closes itself when the sweep merges; nothing else is owed on it.
